content.text:
<challenge>
Design and build the strongest Gmail-inspired email application you can.

Recreate the clarity, information density, speed, and familiar workflows of a great modern inbox. Take the implementation as far as you can: choose the stack, scope, visual direction, data model, and technical limits that let you deliver the most convincing complete product.
</challenge>

<essential-outcomes>
The finished application must include:

- A polished, responsive mail shell with a recognizable inbox, navigation, toolbar, search, and account controls.
- A realistic seeded mailbox with varied senders, subjects, timestamps, labels, read states, attachments, threads, and message content.
- Functional mailbox navigation for at least Inbox, Starred, Sent, Drafts, and Trash.
- Working message selection, read/unread state, starring, archiving, deleting, and labeling.
- A usable search experience that filters or retrieves relevant mail.
- A message-reading view with a clear conversation hierarchy and useful actions.
- A compose experience with recipients, subject, body, draft behavior, send behavior, and a polished interaction model.
- Responsive behavior that remains coherent and usable on both desktop and mobile.
</essential-outcomes>

<product-depth>
Go beyond a static visual recreation. Interactions should update the interface consistently, preserve state where useful, and make the product feel alive. You may add keyboard shortcuts, bulk actions, category tabs, snoozing, scheduled mail, contact suggestions, rich composition, settings, themes, offline persistence, or any other details that strengthen the experience.

No external email account, authentication, paid service, or API key is required. A fully local product with excellent seeded data and convincing behavior is valid. Do not leave prominent controls as decorative placeholders when a meaningful local interaction can be implemented.
</product-depth>

<creative-freedom>
You have broad freedom over architecture, libraries, layout details, interaction design, copy, and visual polish. Use Gmail as the product reference, but make deliberate decisions and deliver a coherent application rather than a collection of disconnected screens.

Do not explain your design before building it. Make the product and engineering decisions yourself, implement the experience, test the important workflows, and refine it into the best result you can.
</creative-freedom>

<success-criteria>
The result should immediately read as a high-quality email client, reward exploration, and support a convincing end-to-end flow from finding a message to reading, organizing, composing, and sending mail. Visual fidelity matters, but functional depth, consistency, responsiveness, and product judgment matter just as much.
</success-criteria>

Work only inside the current working directory. Do not read, list, search, or edit files outside the current working directory. Treat it as a standalone project root.
During setup, configure your app and package scripts to use port 9349, then use that port for runtime verification.
Use pnpm exclusively if dependency installation or package scripts are needed. Do not use npm.
Set the browser title and the primary visible title to your model name, using only identity information already available to you. Add nothing else to either title.
Run the relevant checks yourself. Do not edit files outside the current working directory.

# Claude Opus 5.5 — mail client

A Gmail-style mail client that runs entirely in the browser. It has no backend and makes no network calls; the mailbox is seeded on first load and persisted to `localStorage`.

## Run

```bash
pnpm install
pnpm dev          # http://localhost:9349
pnpm build        # typecheck + production build
pnpm preview      # serve dist on 9349
pnpm test:e2e     # Playwright workflows against a running dev server (uses local Chrome)
```

## What works

- **Folders:** Inbox (with Primary, Promotions, Social and Updates tabs, or Important/Unread/Starred-first sorting), Starred, Snoozed, Important, Sent, Scheduled, Drafts, All Mail, Spam, Trash. User labels have colors, a context menu, and drag-a-row-onto-label.
- **List:** checkbox selection (with shift-range), select-all-in-view banner, and bulk archive/delete/spam/read/unread/snooze/move/label/important/mute. Also stars, importance markers, attachment chips, pagination, three densities, and a split reading pane (right or bottom, resizable).
- **Search:** operators (`from:`, `to:`, `subject:`, `has:attachment`, `is:unread|starred|important|snoozed`, `in:`, `label:`, `before:`/`after:`/`older_than:`/`newer_than:`, `-negation`, `"phrases"`, `OR`), an advanced search form, and live suggestions.
- **Threads:** collapsible conversation with expand/collapse all, quoted-text toggle, per-message reply/forward/star/show original. Also inline reply, print, attachment viewer (images, docs, PDF download, calendar RSVP), and j/k between threads.
- **Compose:** multiple windows (minimize/expand/full screen), recipient chips with contact autocomplete, Cc/Bcc, and a rich editor (fonts, sizes, color, lists, links, emoji, quote, indent). Also attachments, signature, draft autosave, undo send, schedule send, and discard.
- **Time-based behavior:** snoozed mail returns on time, scheduled mail is delivered, contacts reply to what you send, and new mail trickles in with notifications.
- **Settings:** light/dark/system theme, density, inbox type, reading pane, undo-send window, signature, keyboard shortcuts toggle, and a reset option for the demo mailbox.
- **Keyboard:** Gmail-style shortcuts; press `?` for the full list.
- **Mobile:** drawer navigation, avatar-tap and long-press selection, swipe to archive, a shrinking Compose FAB, and full-screen thread, reply and compose views.

content.text:
The mail app is done and running at http://localhost:9349. The typecheck and production build are clean, and all 51 browser tests pass across three Playwright suites, desktop and mobile, with no console errors. The browser title and the visible header both read exactly "Claude Opus 5.5".

**What you get**
- **Folders:** Inbox (with Primary, Promotions, Social and Updates tabs), Starred, Snoozed, Important, Sent, Scheduled, Drafts, All Mail, Spam and Trash. Labels have colors, and you can drag a row onto a label in the sidebar.
- **List:** shift-click range selection, a "select all N conversations" banner, and bulk archive, delete, spam, read/unread, snooze, move, label, important and mute. There's pagination, three densities, and a resizable reading pane on the right or bottom.
- **Search:** Gmail operators (`from:`, `to:`, `subject:`, `has:attachment`, `is:`, `in:`, `label:`, date filters, `-negation`, quoted phrases, `OR`), plus an advanced search form and live suggestions.
- **Threads:** collapsible conversations, quoted-text toggle, inline reply and forward, print, and `j`/`k` to move between threads. Attachments open in a viewer that handles images, documents (with PDF download) and calendar invites with working RSVP buttons.
- **Compose:** multiple windows (minimize, full screen), recipient chips with contact autocomplete, Cc/Bcc, and a rich editor with formatting, links and emoji. Drafts autosave, and there's a signature, undo send and schedule send.
- **Things that happen over time:** snoozed mail comes back, scheduled mail gets sent, contacts reply to what you send, and new mail arrives with a notification.
- **Settings:** light, dark or system theme, density, inbox sorting, reading pane position, undo-send delay, signature and a mailbox reset. Everything is saved in the browser and works offline; there are no external services.
- **Mobile:** drawer navigation, long-press or avatar tap to select, swipe to archive, a Compose button that shrinks as you scroll, and full-screen reading and compose.
- **Keyboard:** full Gmail-style shortcuts; press `?` in the app for the list.

**Fixed in this last pass**
- `OR` search wasn't actually supported, so I built it. It works like Gmail: `from:linda OR from:hannah is:starred` means (Linda or Hannah) and starred.
- `b`, `l` and `v` did nothing when a row was only highlighted with `j`/`k` and not ticked. They now select that row and open the snooze, label or move menu.
- The shortcuts help listed `b` as "snooze until tomorrow" (it opens the snooze menu) and left out some bindings. It now matches what the keys do.
- Selecting a mix of snoozed and normal conversations showed only Unsnooze. It now shows Snooze unless every selected conversation is snoozed.
- Two tests failed only because of how they matched text, not because of app bugs. I fixed the tests and added new ones for `OR` and the keyboard menus.

**Scripts:** `pnpm dev` runs on 9349. `pnpm build`, `pnpm preview` and `pnpm typecheck` do what they say. `pnpm test:e2e` runs all three suites against the running dev server using your local Chrome.

One cost to know about: the icon font is about 4 MB because the package ships the full set of Material Symbols. That's fine locally, but it's the first thing to cut down to only the icons used if this ever gets deployed.

**What you get**
- **Folders:** Inbox (with Primary, Promotions, Social and Updates tabs), Starred, Snoozed, Important, Sent, Scheduled, Drafts, All Mail, Spam and Trash. Labels have colors, and you can drag a row onto a label in the sidebar.
- **List:** shift-click range selection, a "select all N conversations" banner, and bulk archive, delete, spam, read/unread, snooze, move, label, important and mute. There's pagination, three densities, and a resizable reading pane on the right or bottom.
- **Search:** Gmail operators (`from:`, `to:`, `subject:`, `has:attachment`, `is:`, `in:`, `label:`, date filters, `-negation`, quoted phrases, `OR`), plus an advanced search form and live suggestions.
- **Threads:** collapsible conversations, quoted-text toggle, inline reply and forward, print, and `j`/`k` to move between threads. Attachments open in a viewer that handles images, documents (with PDF download) and calendar invites with working RSVP buttons.
- **Compose:** multiple windows (minimize, full screen), recipient chips with contact autocomplete, Cc/Bcc, and a rich editor with formatting, links and emoji. Drafts autosave, and there's a signature, undo send and schedule send.
- **Things that happen over time:** snoozed mail comes back, scheduled mail gets sent, contacts reply to what you send, and new mail arrives with a notification.
- **Settings:** light, dark or system theme, density, inbox sorting, reading pane position, undo-send delay, signature and a mailbox reset. Everything is saved in the browser and works offline; there are no external services.
- **Mobile:** drawer navigation, long-press or avatar tap to select, swipe to archive, a Compose button that shrinks as you scroll, and full-screen reading and compose.
- **Keyboard:** full Gmail-style shortcuts; press `?` in the app for the list.

**Fixed in this last pass**
- `OR` search wasn't actually supported, so I built it. It works like Gmail: `from:linda OR from:hannah is:starred` means (Linda or Hannah) and starred.
- `b`, `l` and `v` did nothing when a row was only highlighted with `j`/`k` and not ticked. They now select that row and open the snooze, label or move menu.
- The shortcuts help listed `b` as "snooze until tomorrow" (it opens the snooze menu) and left out some bindings. It now matches what the keys do.
- Selecting a mix of snoozed and normal conversations showed only Unsnooze. It now shows Snooze unless every selected conversation is snoozed.
- Two tests failed only because of how they matched text, not because of app bugs. I fixed the tests and added new ones for `OR` and the keyboard menus.

**Scripts:** `pnpm dev` runs on 9349. `pnpm build`, `pnpm preview` and `pnpm typecheck` do what they say. `pnpm test:e2e` runs all three suites against the running dev server using your local Chrome.

One cost to know about: the icon font is about 4 MB because the package ships the full set of Material Symbols. That's fine locally, but it's the first thing to cut down to only the icons used if this ever gets deployed.
